subject: Go-live readiness: bake window, traffic shift plan, and smoke results
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.com, cloudops@jetstream.io
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Go-live readiness: bake window, traffic shift plan, and smoke results

Hi team —

We're on track for the private deployment activation today. Proposed short "bake" window: 11:00-13:00 PDT. During that time we'll shift traffic in phased increments and run targeted smoke tests. Key asks: please confirm the two-phase traffic-shift cadence below and whether Jetstream can keep the ingress ACLs pinned during the bake.

Proposed plan (high level):
1) Pre-cutover (10:30-10:50): validation of OVN routes, firewall rules, and K8s probe success; confirm certificate rollout.
2) Bake window (11:00-13:00): phased traffic shift 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 15-20m steady-state between steps.
3) During each phase run the smoke checklist (attached runbook_v3.pdf):
   - connectivity and auth checks
   - KV-cache priming (see commands in runbook)
   - latency percentile sampling (p50/p95/p99)
   - error-rate threshold: >1.5% 5m rolling triggers rollback
4) Observability sampling: short traces captured for 1% of requests, ingest to dev traces for quick look.
5) Rollback: immediate rollback to previous routing if any SLI breaches or significant tail latency.

Attachments: runbook_v3.pdf (full step-by-step), smoke_results_20270611.csv (blank template), kvcache_warmup_log.txt (log template).

If Acme ops confirms the phased traffic shift, we'll begin the pre-cutover checks at 10:30.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Engineering Lead, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: cloudops@jetstream.io
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Go-live readiness: bake window, traffic shift plan, and smoke results

Tessa —

Confirming we can do the phased shift. A couple of notes from our side:
- We prefer a 3-step shift (10% -> 40% -> 100%) with a 20m hold between each to watch backend saturation.
- Please provide the exact HTTP health-check endpoints you will hit for priming so our WAF can whitelist them for the bake window.
- We'll keep ACLs pinned but need a short IP allowlist for Jetstream to push traffic during the first phase (sending IPs in a follow-up).

Also, can you confirm the rollback signal — is it strictly error-rate >1.5% or also >200ms p99 for more than 5 minutes? We want to align alarms with our pager thresholds.

Thanks —
Anjali Kapoor
Site Reliability, Acme Corp
ops@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, cloudops@jetstream.io
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Go-live readiness: bake window, traffic shift plan, and smoke results

Thanks Anjali — noted on the 3-step shift. Quick answers and concrete checks below.

Rollback signals (we'll use combined triggers):
- Error rate: >1.5% rolling 5m OR
- p99 latency >200ms rolling 5m OR
- Any auth-failure spike or sustained 500s.

Health-check endpoints (will be used for priming and periodic checks):
- /health/readiness (200 + JSON {status: "ok"})
- /internal/ping (200 plain text)
- /kv/prime-status (200 + CSV of warmed shards)

KV cache priming (commands we run during pre-cutover and after each shift):
- priming job: /ops/prime-kv --mode=batch --shards=all --parallel=8  (logs to kvcache_warmup_log.txt)
- Expected warmup time: ~8-12 minutes for the working set; we recommend starting priming at the tail of the pre-cutover window so first phase sees warmed caches.

Smoke checklist highlights (from runbook_v3.pdf):
- Basic auth flows (token exchange), sample queries, embedding calls, and cold-start latency checks.
- Observability: enable 1% trace sampling, ingest to temporary dev-trace dataset for 30m.
- Traffic shaping: Jetstream should apply the 10/40/100 weighting over routes; Redwood will verify via route metrics and token-level traces.

Attachments: smoke_results_20270611.csv (we'll populate during the bake), kvcache_warmup_log.txt (placeholder). I'll post incremental updates in this thread during the bake.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Go-live readiness: bake window, traffic shift plan, and smoke results

Quick post-bake summary (11:00-13:10) — happy to report the activation completed and initial smoke checks passed. High level:

What we ran:
- Phase schedule: 10% (11:03-11:23), 40% (11:44-12:04), 100% (12:25-13:10). Jetstream held weighting as requested.
- KV priming: batch priming completed before first phase; kvcache_warmup_log.txt attached. Warm set reached ~92% hit rate by the 2nd phase.
- Latency: p50=12ms p95=68ms p99=180ms during 100% steady-state. No p99 breaches >200ms.
- Error rates: peaked at 0.9% transient during the first 10m of the 40% ramp, stabilized to 0.2%.
- Observability: 1% traces collected and uploaded; no auth regressions.

Open items / notes:
- Acme WAF team briefly blocked one warming endpoint (internal/ping) during priming; we coordinated and whitelist was added at 11:08 which delayed warming by ~4 minutes.
- We'll keep an elevated sampling window for the next 24h and revert trace retention after 36h.

Next steps:
- Monitor for 24h and then hand off to Acme for business acceptance.
- Post-mortem if any customer-facing anomalies appear in the next 12h.

Attachments: smoke_results_20270611.csv (completed), kvcache_warmup_log.txt (full run).

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
